statistic: 43% of US franchise dealership website domains publish no mail record. Of 17,659 domains taken from manufacturer dealer locators, 7,680 accept no email at the website domain, so a guessed address bounces before any deliverability question arises.
Microsoft 365 is the largest single destination for dealership mail, at 30% of the 8,038 dealer domains that receive email (2,396 domains).
Google Workspace covers 13% of dealer domains that receive email (1,022 domains).
11% of dealer domains that receive email sit behind a security gateway such as Mimecast, Barracuda, Proofpoint, AppRiver, Sophos or TitanHQ. Mimecast alone fronts 5% (382 domains).

Measured by people rather than domains, Microsoft 365 received 45% of contacts in a 10,760-contact dealership campaign sample, and Google Workspace 20%. Larger dealer groups run more staff per domain, which is why the people-weighted share is higher than the domain share.
9% of dealer domains that receive email use GoDaddy-hosted mail, and a further 35% resolve to other or self-managed hosts.
Google Workspace recipients replied to dealership cold email at 1.09% across 43,302 sends from Google-hosted inboxes with identical copy and sequence.
Microsoft 365 recipients replied at 0.07% on the same campaigns, a 14.8x gap against Google Workspace recipients.

On Google Workspace, positive and negative replies arrived in equal numbers, 75 to 75. On Microsoft 365 the ratio was 24 positives to 5 declines, which is the signature of mail not being seen rather than a less interested audience.
Barracuda-fronted recipients who received the mail replied at 2.1% to 2.8% of delivered messages, the highest delivered reply rate of any gateway in the study.
Sophos-fronted recipients replied at 2.4% to 3.0% of delivered messages, on a small sample.
No replies were observed from Proofpoint-fronted or Mimecast-fronted dealership recipients across the study.

section: Bounces that are policy, not bad data
statistic: Mimecast rejected 52% of dealership cold emails in one sending workspace and 72% in another, and produced zero replies.

section: Bounces that are policy, not bad data
statistic: Those Mimecast-rejected addresses had been marked deliverable by a paid email verification service before the campaign. A verifier tests whether a mailbox exists, not whether a gateway will accept an unknown sender.

section: Bounces that are policy, not bad data
statistic: Barracuda bounced 7% to 12% of sends and then delivered the remainder into inboxes that replied at the study's best rate, so a high bounce figure from Barracuda is filtering, not a dead list.

section: Bounces that are policy, not bad data
statistic: Microsoft 365 recipients bounced at 2.6% to 4.4% of sends, a low bounce rate paired with the lowest reply rate, which is why bounce rate alone misreads Microsoft-hosted dealers.
Volkswagen, GMC and Audi dealers are the most Microsoft 365-heavy franchises at 43%, 43% and 41% of domains respectively.
BMW and Mercedes-Benz dealers are the most likely to sit behind a security gateway, at 24% and 23% of domains.
Ford dealers are the least Microsoft-heavy major franchise at 22% Microsoft 365 and only 5% behind a security gateway.
California is the most Microsoft-heavy state, with 41% of dealer domains on Microsoft 365, ten points above the next state.
Virginia and Indiana are the least Microsoft-heavy states at 16% and 17%, and Virginia dealers use Google Workspace (18%) more often than Microsoft 365.
New York dealers have the highest Google Workspace share of any large state at 24% of domains.

44% of 221 hand-read negative or stale replies were about the contact rather than the offer: retired, left the store, sold the dealership or changed roles. The list had passed every structural check before sending.
Reading the audit as a whole, the receiving gateway explained more of the variation in outcome than the copy did: the same sequence produced a 1.09% reply rate on one gateway and 0.07% on another.
75% of the 8,032 franchise dealer domains that receive mail publish an SPF record, and 37% end it with a hard fail.
47% of mail-receiving dealer domains publish a DMARC record; 23% enforce it with p=quarantine or p=reject, and 8% reject outright. 24% run the monitoring-only p=none.
32% of mail-receiving dealer domains publish SPF with no DMARC record at all, the configuration that leaves the dealership's From address open to spoofing.
Dealers behind a security gateway enforce DMARC at 46% of domains; Microsoft 365 dealers at 34%; Google Workspace dealers at 15%, and only 7% of Google-hosted dealers hard-fail SPF.
Mercedes-Benz stores enforce DMARC at 40% of domains and Ford stores at 6%, among brands with 150 or more dealer domains receiving mail.
Florida dealers enforce DMARC at 44% of domains and Michigan dealers at 12%, among states with 100 or more dealer domains receiving mail.
